taxonomy.note: For a long time Plesiosaurus was a wastebasket genus. After revision it contains only one valid species, the type species P. dolichodeirus.

diet.note: Inferred from tooth form: plesiosauroid teeth pierced small soft-bodied prey such as fish and cephalopods.

timeRange.note: The holotype comes from the late Sinemurian (Charmouth Mudstone). The Ma values are the ICS v2024/12 Sinemurian boundaries. PBDB also has two loosely dated records (Hettangian to Pliensbachian) not used here.

discovery.note: The genus Plesiosaurus was named by De la Beche & Conybeare in 1821; Conybeare named the species P. dolichodeirus in 1824.

text.en: Plesiosaurus was not a dinosaur but a marine reptile that swam in the seas over what is now southern England in the Early Jurassic. It had a long neck, and its pointed teeth were good for piercing small, soft prey such as fish and squid-like animals. Mary Anning found the complete skeleton that defines the species at Lyme Regis.
Its species name dolichodeirus comes from Greek words for 'long' and 'neck'.
The complete skeleton that defines the species was discovered and collected by Mary Anning.
